headline: Mechanical force
body: builds bone through a named pathway

headline: Your bones
body: contain cells called *osteocytes*. | They sit inside the bone matrix and do one job: detect mechanical stress. | They convert physical force into chemical signals.
punch: Your skeleton has dedicated force sensors.

headline: When you load bone
body: Osteocytes sense the strain. | They secrete *nitric oxide* and *PGE2*. | Those two block a protein called **sclerostin**, coded by the *SOST* gene.

headline: Sclerostin
body: is a brake on bone formation. | It blocks the *Wnt* pathway, which is the main anabolic signal for bone. | Less sclerostin means more Wnt.
punch: Loading works by removing a brake, not adding a gas pedal.

headline: And more Wnt
body: increases the number of cells that produce bone. | It also suppresses bone resorption at the same time. | Both directions at once.

headline: This was measured
body: Robling and colleagues, Journal of Biological Chemistry, 2008. | Mechanical stimulation of bone in vivo reduced osteocyte Sost and sclerostin expression. | Direct measurement of the gene response to load.
punch: Without sclerostin downregulation there is no bone growth from mechanical stress.

headline: Cartilage does it too
body: *Chondrocytes* sense load through a three tier cascade. | Ion channels at the membrane. Then intracellular signalling. Then gene expression.

headline: The receptor doing it
body: is *estrogen receptor alpha*. | It works as a mechanotransducer with no estrogen bound to it at all. | Completely separate from its hormone job.
punch: Your estrogen receptor moonlights as a strain gauge.

headline: Loading in range
body: maintains ER alpha expression. | That keeps *COL2* and *SOX9* running, which are the genes for cartilage identity. | The tissue is told to keep being cartilage.
punch: Right amount of load builds tissue.

headline: Loading above it
body: **inhibits** ER alpha expression. | COL2 and SOX9 get downregulated. | **MMP13** and **ADAMTS4** get upregulated. Those are cartilage degrading enzymes.
punch: Same tissue. Same receptor. Opposite result.

headline: Which means
body: Loading is not binary. It has a dose response curve. | There is a window where force builds and a level above it where the same tissue breaks itself down. | Both halves are real and measured.
punch: The variable is magnitude. Not whether you load.

headline: And adults
body: are not exempt from this. | Blocking the *P2Y2* receptor increased periosteal bone formation under exercise loading in adult mice. | Adult bone still responds to mechanical signals.
punch: Your skeleton never stops listening to force.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms. Real citations. No protocols.
